locator: Google Material 3 Expressive research; attention, preference, usability, accessibility, familiarity, and context limits
summary: Google reports extensive research in which purposeful color, shape, size, motion, and containment improved attention and preference, while unfamiliar or unlabeled structures harmed usability. The transferable lesson is evidence-led expression balanced with recognizable interaction patterns and accessibility—not adoption of Material components or maximal styling.
